analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Vision is a genuine growth story in underpenetrated East India consumer electronics retail — this was a brilliant SMILE stock at ₹200–500 Cr market cap, but at ₹6,759 Cr and 61x P/E, the multibagger opportunity has already been captured. With free cash flow bleeding at -₹78 Cr and worsening, the business is consuming capital faster than it generates it, making this a speculative bet at a value investor's worst enemy — a growth premium price.
key_strengths: Strong 36% revenue CAGR (₹899 Cr → ₹2,260 Cr in 3 years) with net profit growing even faster at 44.1% CAGR
ROCE of 29.95% signals genuine capital efficiency in the store-level economics despite thin margins
First-mover regional dominance in Bihar/East India — a structurally underpenetrated, aspirational consumption market
key_risks: Free cash flow is -₹78 Cr in FY25 and worsening every year (was +₹13 Cr in FY22) — rapid store expansion is destroying cash
P/E of 61x with thin 6.57% operating margins leaves zero margin of safety; any growth disappointment could halve the stock
Debt risen sharply to ₹480 Cr (D/E 0.65) with ₹32 Cr annual finance costs eating into thin profits
red_flags: Market cap ₹6,759 Cr — 6x outside my sweet spot; the multibagger has already been made by someone else
Promoter holding at 47.14% — below my non-negotiable 50% threshold, showing declining skin-in-the-game
Operating cash flow turned negative in FY24 (-₹6 Cr) and collapsed to -₹41 Cr in FY25 — the business model is not self-funding at this growth rate
P/E 61x vs my target entry of 8–15x; Forward P/E 41x is still 2–3x my comfort zone
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aditya Vision is the story I wish I had found in 2018 when it was a ₹300 Cr market cap regional retailer in Patna — that would have been a classic SMILE candidate. Today at ₹6,759 Cr, it is priced as if every future store opening is already in the price. The business is genuinely good: 36% revenue CAGR, 44% net profit CAGR, and ROCE of nearly 30% suggest strong unit economics at the store level. But consumer electronics retail is structurally a 6–7% operating margin business — there is no pricing power here, no brand moat, just execution. At 61x P/E on 6.57% operating margins, the market is paying a technology company multiple for a retail distributor.

The cash flow story is the real dealbreaker for me. Operating cash flow has gone from +₹32 Cr in FY22 to -₹41 Cr in FY25 as working capital devours the growth. Free cash flow at -₹78 Cr means every new store is being funded by debt (₹480 Cr, D/E 0.65) and equity raises — not internal accruals. This is the opposite of what I look for: a business that gets stronger as it scales, not one that needs constant external capital. Promoter holding slipping below 50% reinforces my concern. I want to find the next Aditya Vision, not buy this one at the peak.
